question: Summer, a single individual, had a net operating loss of $20,000 three years ago. A Code Sec. 1244 stock loss made up three-fourths of that loss. Summer had no taxable income from that year until the current year. In the current year, Summer has gross income of $80,000 and sustains another loss of $50,000 on Code Sec. 1244 stock. Assuming that Summer can carry the entire $20,000 net operating loss to the current year, what is the amount and character of the Code Sec. 1244 loss that Summer can deduct for the current year?
options: $20,000 capital loss.
$30,000 ordinary loss.
$40,000 capital loss.
$40,000 ordinary loss.
$30,000 capital loss.
$35,000 ordinary loss.
$50,000 capital loss.
$20,000 ordinary loss.
$50,000 ordinary loss.
$35,000 capital loss.
model_outputs: We refer to Wikipedia articles on taxation for help. Under Section 1244, the amount of a capital loss can be carried forward indefinitely if it was incurred before January 1, 1986. If a loss was sustained after January 1, 1986, it cannot be carried forward. This means that if a loss was sustained after 1986, it will be treated as an ordinary loss. Therefore, the amount and character of the Code Sec. 1244 loss that Summer can deduct for the current year depends on whether the loss was sustained before or after January 1, 1986. Since Summer has already sustained a capital loss of $20,000 in 2017, which is before January 1, 1986, the amount of the Code Sec. 1244 loss that Summer can deduct for the current year is $20,000, which is a capital loss. The answer is (A).
